extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examining and drafting Office actions involving restriction requirements, double patenting rejections, and treatment of copending applications/references (35 U.S.C. 102(e), 103(a), species/genus/election practice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copending application prior art requirement (common assignee/inventor)
rubrics_metrics.description: A copending application or patent/patent application publication used as a 35 U.S.C. 102(e) reference must have either a common assignee or at least one common inventor with the instant application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph is used to reject over a patent or patent application publication with an earlier filing date that discloses but does not claim the same invention. Insert either --assignee-- or --inventor-- in bracket 3. If the applied reference has a common [assignee/inventor] it constitutes prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) based upon its earlier effective U.S. filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of amended 35 U.S.C. 102(e) (AIPA / post-2000) to determine prior art date
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as amended by the American Inventors Protection Act (AIPA) and the Intellectual Property and High Technology Technical Amendments Act of 2002 (form paragraph 7.12) to determine a copending application's 102(e) prior art date, except for certain international-application-derived references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the copending application reference is based directly or indirectly from an international application having an international filing date prior to November 29, 2000, use pre-AIPA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) (form paragraph 7.12.01). See Examiner Notes for form paragraphs 7.12 and 7.12.01 for assistance in determining the correct 102(e) date.

rubrics_metrics.name: When an international-application-derived reference is pre-AIPA
rubrics_metrics.description: If the copending reference is a national stage of an international application (35 U.S.C. 371) or a continuing application claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, or 365(c) to an international application with an international filing date prior to November 29, 2000, apply pre-AIPA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) (form paragraph 7.12.01).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Examiner Notes for form paragraph 7.12.01 to determine the 35 U.S.C. 102(e) date. A benefit claim to a U.S. patent of an earlier-filed international application with an international filing date prior to Nov. 29, 2000, may only result in an effective U.S. filing date as of the date the 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(1),(2),(4) requirements were fulfilled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not treat certain international publications as 102(e) prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reference is a publication of an international application with an international filing date prior to November 29, 2000, that did not designate the United States or was not published in English by WIPO, do not treat it as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such references may be applied under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (b) as of their publication date. See form paragraphs 7.08 and 7.09. Do not use form paragraph 7.15.02 in that situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of priority/benefit claims in determining 102(e) date
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining the 102(e) date, consider priority/benefit claims to earlier-filed U.S. provisional applications under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), U.S. nonprovisional applications under 35 U.S.C. 120 or 121, and international applications under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121 or 365(c) if the subject matter used to make the rejection is appropriately supported in the earlier-filed application's disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT consider any priority/benefit claims to U.S. applications which are filed before an international application that has an international filing date prior to Nov. 29, 2000. Do NOT consider foreign priority claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) and 365(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overcoming 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) may be overcome by a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that any invention disclosed but not claimed in the reference was derived from the inventor of the instant application (not an invention 'by another'), or by an appropriate showing under 37 CFR 1.131 (date of invention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also consider a showing under 37 CFR 1.131 or other appropriate evidence. If evidence indicates derivation or earlier invention date, the rejection may be withdrawn. Examiner Notes: ensure supporting factual basis is of record when making or withdrawing such rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) based on copending application (¶7.21.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims provisionally rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being obvious over a copending application with an earlier effective U.S. filing date that has a common assignee or at least one common inventor; this is a presumption of future publication or patenting of the copending application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provisional rejection might be overcome by a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 (derivation), a showing of an invention date under 37 CFR 1.131, or by showing the copending application is disqualified under 35 U.S.C. 103(c). Do not use this form paragraph for applications pending on or after Dec. 10, 2004 when the copending application is disqualified under 35 U.S.C. 103(c) as prior art in a 103(a) rejection (see MPEP §706.02(l)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overcoming 35 U.S.C. 103(a) copending-application provisional rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: A 103(a) provisional rejection based on a copending application can be overcome by derivation evidence (37 CFR 1.132), showing an earlier invention date (37 CFR 1.131), or showing disqualification of the copending application under 35 U.S.C. 103(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively, an oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.130 that the application and reference are currently owned by the same party and that the named inventor is the prior inventor, together with a terminal disclaimer in accordance with 37 CFR 1.321(c), may be used to overcome the rejection. See MPEP §706.02(l)(1) and (2).

rubrics_metrics.name: When to use 35 U.S.C. 102(e) vs. 102(a)/(b) for references
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reference qualifies as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (b), then form paragraph 7.21 (which applies to 102(e) references) should not be used; use the appropriate form paragraphs for 102(a) or (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if a reference is qualifying under 102(a)/(b) (e.g., by publication date), do not treat it solely as a 102(e) earlier-filing reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to submit certain double patenting actions to Technology Center Director
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Office action containing a rejection on the ground of double patenting which relies on the parent application rejecting claims in a divisional or continuing application filed because of a restriction requirement under 35 U.S.C. 121 (including election of species) must be submitted to the Technology Center Director (TCD) for approval prior to mailing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the TCD disapproves the double patenting rejection, it shall not be mailed and other appropriate action shall be taken. See MPEP §1003.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of improper joinder under 35 U.S.C. 121
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 121 last sentence, the validity of a patent shall not be questioned for failure of the Director to require the application to be restricted to one invention; thus no patent can be held void for improper joinder of inventions claimed therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits challenges to a patent's validity based solely on alleged improper joinder where the Office failed to require restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principles for determination of distinctness/independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinctness/independence summarized: (A) where inventions are independent (no disclosed relation), restriction ordinarily proper; (B) where related as disclosed but distinct as claimed, restriction may be proper; (C) where related as disclosed but not distinct as claimed, restriction is never proper; (D) a reasonable number of species may be claimed where there is an allowable generic claim (37 CFR 1.141).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where restriction is required by the Office, double patenting cannot be held — so ensure requirement is not made where related inventions as claimed are not distinct. See referenced MPEP sections for details (§806.06, §806.05-§806.05(j), §806.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare claimed matter (claimed subject matter controls)
rubrics_metrics.description: In double patenting and restriction inquiries, it is the claimed subject matter that is considered and must be compared to determine distinctness or independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A provisional election of a single species may be required where only generic claims are presented and the generic claims recite so many species that an unduly extensive and burdensome search is necessary. See MPEP §803.02 and §808.01(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-embodiment claims defining same essential features
rubrics_metrics.description: Where claims define the same essential characteristics of a single disclosed embodiment, restriction between those claims should never be required because they are different definitions of the same disclosed subject matter, not distinct inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such claims are voluntarily presented in different applications having at least one common inventor or a common assignee, see MPEP §804-§804.02 for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus and species election/restriction practice
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application includes claims to different embodiments or species that could fall within the scope of a generic claim, restriction between species may be proper if the species are independent or distinct; 37 CFR 1.141 allows an allowable generic claim to link a reasonable number of species embraced thereby.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application contains claims to more than a reasonable number of species, the examiner may require restriction to not more than a reasonable number of species before taking further action (37 CFR 1.146). See MPEP §806.04(d) for definition of generic claim and §806.04(e) for claims that include species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and consequences of an allowable generic claim
rubrics_metrics.description: A generic claim should require no material element additional to those required by the species claims, and each species claim must require all the limitations of the generic claim. Once a generic claim is allowable, species that require all limitations of the generic claim will ordinarily be allowable over the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If some species claims do not require all limitations of the generic claim, see MPEP §821.04(a) for handling. When a generic claim is allowable, rejoinder of species and examination of dependent claims follows 37 CFR 1.104 and MPEP §821.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims vs. species terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims are definitions or descriptions of inventions; claims themselves are never 'species.' A claim may be limited to a single disclosed embodiment (specific/species claim) or may encompass multiple embodiments (genus/generic claim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Species always refer to different embodiments of the invention; species may be independent or related as disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction between mutually exclusive species
rubrics_metrics.description: A restriction to a single species may be proper where two or more species are claimed and they are mutually exclusive (i.e., claims do not overlap in scope).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Species are mutually exclusive if one claim recites limitations disclosed for a first species but not a second, and vice versa; equivalently, the claims must not overlap in scope to require restriction between them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species must be patentably distinct from each other
rubrics_metrics.description: In making restriction requirements among plural species, examiners should group species considered clearly unpatentable over each other and ensure species are patentably distinct when required; otherwise restriction is improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where generic claims are allowable, applicant may claim additional species (37 CFR 1.141). If species are voluntarily presented in different applications (no election required by the Office), investigate whether a double patenting rejection would be appropriate. See MPEP §804.01 and §804.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic claim presented after issuance of species may raise OTDP
rubrics_metrics.description: If a generic claim is presented after issuance of a patent claiming one or more species within the scope of the generic claim, the Office may reject the generic claim on the grounds of obviousness-type double patenting if there is at least one common inventor and the applications/patents are commonly assigned or within joint research agreement exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may overcome such a rejection by filing a terminal disclaimer. See cases cited (In re Goodman; In re Braithwaite) and MPEP §804.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related inventions: distinctness governs restriction and double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more related inventions are claimed, the principal question for a restriction requirement or double patenting rejection is whether the inventions as claimed are distinct: if distinct, restriction may be proper; if not distinct, restriction is never proper. Nondistinct inventions claimed in separate applications or patents generally mandate a double patenting holding, except where additional applications were filed consonant with a restriction requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related inventions in the same statutory class are considered mutually exclusive (not overlapping) if a first invention would not infringe the second and vice versa. See MPEP §806.05 for related-invention examples and tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination vs. subcombination distinctness criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To support a restriction between a combination and a subcombination, both two-way distinctness and reasons for insisting on restriction (e.g., serious search burden) are necessary. The inventions are distinct if: (A) the combination as claimed does not require the particulars of the subcombination as claimed for patentability, and (B) the subcombination can be shown to have utility either by itself or in another materially different combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search-burden evidence (separate classification, status, or field of search) must exist to justify restriction. Examples and diagrams (ABsp, ABbr, Bsp) illustrate when restriction is proper or improper. Use form paragraph 8.15 where appropriate; provide specifics in brackets as instructed by the form paragraph's Examiner Note.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plural combinations requiring common subcombination (linking claim practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application includes a single subcombination required by plural claimed combinations, the subcombination claim is a linking claim and will be examined with the elected combination; claimed plural combinations showing the subcombination's utility in more than one combination support linking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List the linking subcombination in form paragraph 8.12. If elected combination is allowable, reconsider the propriety of restriction and rejoin claims requiring the subcombination as appropriate. See MPEP §809.03 and §821.04(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcombinations usable together: distinctness and restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Two or more claimed subcombinations disclosed as usable together in a single combination are usually restrictable when they do not overlap in scope and are not obvious variants and at least one subcombination is separately usable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restriction is proper only when there would be a serious burden if restriction were not required, evidenced by separate classification, status, or field of search. Examiner must show by example that one subcombination has utility other than in the disclosed combination. If applicant proves the suggested other use cannot be accomplished, the burden shifts to the examiner to document a viable alternative or withdraw the requirement. Use form paragraph 8.16 for restriction requirements between subcombinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden on examiner to suggest separate utility and rejoinder practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner has the burden to suggest an example of separate utility for subcombinations or subcombinations usable together; if applicant disproves the suggested utility, examiner must document an alternative viable use or withdraw the restriction requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon determining that all claims directed to an elected combination invention are allowable, the examiner must reconsider the propriety of the restriction requirement and rejoin claims as required. If a subcombination is elected and found allowable, nonelected claims requiring all limitations of the allowable claim will be rejoined in accordance with MPEP §821.04.
